header.running_head: Enduring Injuries while in Jihaad in the path of Allaah

blocks.text: The Eye of Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan (RA) is Injured During the Battle at Taa'if

Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Ubayd Thaqafi (RA) reports, "During the battle at Taa'if, I spotted Abu Sufyaan bin Harb (RA) sitting and eating on the wall of Abu Ya'la. I shot an arrow at him, which struck his eye. He then went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, 'This eye of mine has been injured in the path of Allaah." Rasulullaah ﷺ said to him, 'If you wish, I could pray to Allaah to return the eye to you. If you wish otherwise, you could have Jannah (in return for your injury).' Abu Sufyaan (RA) replied, 'Let it be Jannah instead.'"[^1]
The Wounds Sustained to the Eyes of Hadhrat Qataadah bin Nu'maan (RA) and Hadhrat Rifaa'ah bin Raafi (RA) During the Battle of Badr

Hadhrat Qataadah bin Nu'maan (RA) narrates that when his eye was injured during the Battle of Badr, his eyeball hung on his cheek and the Sahabah (RA) wanted to cut it off. The rest of the Hadith will be quoted in the chapter concerning the manner in which the Sahabah (RA) received assistance.[^2]

Hadhrat Rifaa'ah bin Raafi (RA) says, "The Mushrikeen amassed around Umayyah bin Khalaf during the Battle of Badr as we approached him. When I noticed that a portion of his armour was broken below his armpit, I struck the area with my sword. I was also struck by an arrow during the Battle of Badr because of which my eye was ruptured. Rasulullaah ﷺ applied some of his saliva to the eye and prayed for me. I then experienced absolutely no pain."[^3]
The Incident of Hadhrat Raafi bin Khadeej (RA) and two other Sahabah (RA) from the Banu Abdul Ash'hal Tribe

The incident reported by Hadhrat Yahya bin Abdul Hameed has already passed[^4] in which he narrates from his grandfather that an arrow struck Hadhrat Raafi bin Khadeej (RA) in the chest during either the Battle of Uhud or the Battle of Hunayn[^5]. He then went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and asked him to remove the arrow. In the same chapter entitled "Enduring Injuries and Illness when Inviting People Towards Allaah", another narration from Hadhrat Abu Saa'ib t[^6] states that a man from the Banu Abdul Ash'hal tribe reported, "My brother and I participated in the Battle of Uhud and we both returned wounded.
